sources.entry: ShellHub - Modern SSH server for remotely accessing linux devices via command line (using any SSH client) or web-based user interface (alternative to sshd). (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: ShellHub is a self-hostable SSH gateway that lets you reach Linux devices behind NAT or firewalls through a server, using any SSH client or a browser-based terminal.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a small agent on each device that dials out to the ShellHub server, so the device needs no public IP or inbound port. Users connect through the server with ssh, scp, sftp, or the web console. Each SSH login is tied to a named team member rather than a copied key in authorized_keys, and removing a person ends their access to all devices. Access Policies are described as default-deny rules controlling which users reach which devices and as which Linux user, and a policy can require a fresh sign-in before each session. ShellHub logs every connection with user, source IP, and device, and devices can be grouped with tags. Self-hosting is done with Docker Compose via make start; the README also mentions a provisioning key for enrolling many devices.
use_cases: remote SSH access to servers behind NAT or firewalls
managing fleets of embedded Linux devices in the field
replacing shared authorized_keys with per-person SSH access
auditing who logged into which server
centralized SSH access control for a team
how_to_run: Open http://<host>/setup to create the admin account and namespace
On each device: curl -sSf http://<host>/install.sh | sh
Enter the pairing code shown by the agent in the console, then connect with ssh <user>@<device>.<namespace>.<host>
notable: Agent dials out, so devices behind NAT need no public IP or inbound port
Works with standard SSH clients (OpenSSH, PuTTY) plus scp, sftp, and port forwarding
Per-person SSH identities with central revocation
Default-deny access policies with optional per-session re-authentication
Packages for Yocto, Buildroot, FreeBSD, and Snap
caveats: Self-hosting requires Docker with Compose and ports 80 and 22 free on the host
MFA, server-side session recording, web endpoints, and multiple namespaces are listed as Cloud or Enterprise editions, not Community
Setup guide for HTTPS and production settings is referenced externally rather than included in the README
